source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Offer hard candy and whole nuts as routine snacks because these foods strengthen chewing skills","B":"Serve whole grapes and round hot-dog slices because chewing ability is mature once a toddler walks","C":"Allow eating while walking or playing because movement does not meaningfully change choking risk","D":"Prepare foods in developmentally safe shapes and sizes and avoid small, hard, round choking hazards"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC recommends preparing food to an age-appropriate size, shape, and texture, avoiding small/hard foods, cutting spherical foods such as grapes into small pieces, and supervising children while eating.
source_row.source_detail: Infant and Toddler Nutrition, Choking Prevention and Potential Choking Hazards; March 11, 2026; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: Which instruction best reduces choking risk when feeding a toddler?
